title: hello again, a new season
content:
my podcast: botanical studies of internet magic
listen on spotify / listen on apple

saying hello, after a while. this is a quick note just to check-in, and share some ideas, intentions, and possibilities for this next season of this podcast / audio channel...

I'd love to hear from you.

send me a note

hello friends, today is july 27th, 2026, and I'm happy to be back here again after many, many months of silence. since my last episode in march, I feel like I've been interdimensional traveling through time and space and place. I want to tell you a little bit about where I've been, and then share some intentions for this upcoming season.

since march, I led season two of labyrinth and taught digital abundance, about business and creativity. and while that was happening, my personal life has been — is being — particleized, like pushed through a particle accelerator into electrons and protons, floating in outer space in the cosmos. I've been in this massive death and birth cycle. it's actually my year of the hang demand — so in november, I'll be entering my death year.

for the last four years, I've had a settled home in istanbul with a partner and a dog that I cherish. and now I have decided to re-enter a nomadic phase alone, as I find a new intimacy with notions of home, belonging, grief, loss. and the most positive thing, perhaps, to come out of this is that my creativity has been thriving explosively, leading me to many new threads and webs of thoughts, ideas, inspirations that I'm excited to share with you.

my podcasting process

you'll notice that on this podcast, I don't really organize in terms of seasons. I don't plan my episodes very far in advance. but since the beginning, I've had seasons of thought, which I would distinguish by the different visual styles of the episode covers.

for the last 34 episodes — one for every year of my life — I've put a lot of effort into making sure that each episode is as clearly articulate and in-depth as possible. because I always think that if you're going to listen to me speak to you in your ears, I don't want to be wasting any time rambling.

so I have had a really convoluted process for making an episode, in which I would make a visual map, I would do a voice map, I would outline in text for hours, I would record and edit and produce. sometimes I would write the transcripts in the early episodes. but this pace and level of intensity meant it would take me between five and eight hours per episode. and that was hard to keep up a weekly rhythm, especially when I'm leading live containers.

I love the practice of being here. I'd love to show up to speak to you more often. so this season, I want to try something new. I'd like to keep the essence of what I've been doing here — the conceptual, process-oriented thinking — as well as introduce a bit more experimentation, a bit more spontaneity and flow and play.

when I first started to podcast in 2024, the idea of podcasting was a really scary thing, because a voice is intimate, it's exposing. I could write and rewrite a sentence ten times, but speaking is embodied. to share my voice literally felt really different and really vulnerable. I remember my heart was pounding the first time I released the first episodes. there's no way to hide myself when I speak.

I've slowly learned to embrace this more, and I want to embrace this more — to allow myself to show up in a more messy, in-process way.

new ideas & possibilities

there have been some questions I've been asking myself as I've been incubating. like: what is a podcast? just like I've been asking, what is a website? what is a book? is a podcast just an audio recording of me talking to myself, into the void, to you — with some coherence, hopefully, and thoughtfulness? how does a podcast live inside time and space in a different way than, say, writing?

in my head I've been playing with some different shapes and forms of what audio could be.

  • could I share ongoing lists of whatever's on my mind that week, of what's inspiring me — kind of like an audio diary?

  • could I plant or throw out tiny wildflower seeds of raw ideas and thoughts about things that might grow later into fully developed episodes?

  • could I be in conversation with collaborators and community members to talk about topics we're both excited about? that will definitely happen.

  • could I use audio as a container for guiding you along creative rituals — for example, could I release meditations, visualizations, or guided practices? a 23-minute drawing practice with my voice as prompts, or a writing practice. what kind of ambient music would I play? personally, I use a lot of green noise, brown noise, white noise, black noise.

  • could I have a q&a, "ask me anything," advice column? if you ask me specific questions, I will do my best to answer them based on my perspective and way of experiencing the world.

  • could I read you things — some old writing, some favorite quotes?

  • could I write you a letter? a letter addressed to you, to myself, to my past and future selves? because as you've probably gathered, sometimes when I record these episodes and think about you — abstract you — you are a part of me, I am a part of you, across time and space, sharing similar journeys, similar experiences, with a level of specificity of what we value and cherish in this life.

  • could I talk to you about what's inspiring me right now — the movies I watched recently, or the books I read? or would that be totally not what you're wanting to hear from an episode about botanical studies of internet magic?

returning to botanical studies

as I think about what this podcast is — how did I begin here, how did I show up in episode one, and how and where am I now — I think this podcast has always meant to be expansive. but the underlying principles and philosophies are about how we grow ecosystems, living worlds, from within, and express that into the external.

how do we be in relationship to internal spaces — the psyche, the imaginal worlds, the creative worlds, the spaces of the body? how do we understand the worlds that live within us through our creative processes, and how do we express that abundance outwards? and even if it doesn't feel like abundance — maybe it just feels like composting soil, or burnt volcanic ash, in my case right now — how do we share even that, tend to those gardens in cycles of death and rebirth?

how do we grow digital ecosystems? how do we build businesses, communities, jungles, tiny urban gardens on top of skyscrapers? how can our botanical studies of internal worlds become magic that we share through the channel of the internet?

this is still a practice about tending, caring, returning to that which we love, and ultimately, homecoming.

intentions

for me, my intentions for this new season of this podcast are shifting away from needing myself to think really hard and be really articulate and concise, into just arriving to be and speak with you — and to trust that my voice can carry something meaningful and true to you, wherever you are.

the last thing I'll say is that I have two small requests for you. first, if there's anything here that sounds exciting for you — if there are any topics you'd like for me to talk about, if you have specific questions or requests you'd like for me to answer — please don't hesitate to reach out to me. drop me a note. I will create a form and link it in the show notes below. I would love to hear from you. second, if you enjoy this podcast, it would be a gift if you could leave me a review — a public reflection for others to find their way here.

as always, you can explore more of my work, my classes, one-on-one advising, on my website. in a few weeks, I'll be starting season three of labyrinth library — there are a few spots left. the best way to keep in touch with me is through my newsletter.

I'm looking forward to speaking to you again very soon.
